issues.problem:
A hidden duplicate can decide which near copies the verdict keeps, and that moves tiers. f7ac37d and r1 never do this.

The mechanism: Sampling.ranked orders parts tied on volume, slot and height by |q(x − x̄)| first (acrossTies, line 523; called at line 562). Here x̄ is the mean of every tied part, hidden ones included. An exact copy made with Ctrl+D (cleaned), or a third copy placed between two near copies, moves x̄ or sits on it. That decides which copy keeps the faces the copies share.

Repro 1 (C09). Type C09's blade core (part 12) to 2.3 long. Ctrl+D the core and nudge it 0.001 along +X (Alt+arrow at the 0.01 step); this copy is cleaned. Every tree reads Sharpening 0.2110 Hard. Now Ctrl+D the copy (an exact copy, cleaned):
- The tree keeps the core and the copy: PartCount +1, Joints 19.13 → 23.41. It plays Sharpening 0.1967 Normal (Hammering 0.3281 → 0.3214).
- f7ac37d and r1 still read 0.2110 Hard.
- A copy placed halfway instead (x + 0.0005, invisible, kept) gives the same 0.1967 on the tree; f7ac37d gives 0.2110.

Repro 2 (plausible #22338, a laminated hilt). Add plate 6 again 0.01 along +Z; it lies inside its plate and the next, cleaned. Then add that copy again exactly. The tree cleans the plate and both copies, so a visible plate drops out of the measure:
- Thinness 0.0252 → 1.0000.
- Hammering 0.1175 Normal → 0.7000 Hard (raw Master); Sharpening 0.0545 → 0.2000 Hard; Smelting 0.1192 → 0.0885.
- cutIndex 0.3971 → 0.6200.
- f7ac37d and r1: 0.1175, cutIndex 0.3971.

Repro 3 (#1851, a laminate, z 0.005): Hammering 0.1983 Normal → 0.2035 Hard.

Corpus (work/nearcopy.luau). Each part was given a copy 0.001, 0.002, 0.005 or 0.01 along X or Z; where the verdict cleaned one of the pair, an exact copy of that one was added.
- Every 25th plausible design, two samples (2,644 designs): 12,328 cases, 3,307 swaps. G moved in 2,377 cases on 1,220 designs, by up to 0.5825. A played tier changed in 107 cases on 71 designs (fullers 65, laminated hilts 26, ribbed 6, laminates 5, plate edges 2, C09 ribs 2, bevel 1).

SPEC statements this makes false:
- §4.4 line 1096: 'a hidden part steers none of the physics a player is shown (… cutIndex)'.
- §4.4 (947–955), §5's third limit (1378–1380), O11 (j) and §0.5 (114): 'it can decide which of two near copies is kept … G the same (where measured)'. In fact it can clean both copies, moves G by up to 0.58 and changes tiers.
- §5's promise: the kept in-between copy is an invisible construction choice outside the four limits.
issues.fix:
Tried in var/fixa (out/fixa_src.diff): order the verdict's ties by place alone. The measure keeps |q| first, because its ties are kept parts only.

- acrossTies gains a parameter `signed: boolean`, and its last line becomes `if signed then kp[3], kp[4], kp[5], kp[6] = qx, qx, qz, qz else kp[3], kp[4], kp[5], kp[6] = abs(qx), qx, abs(qz), qz end`.
- Sampling.ranked calls `acrossTies(parts, keys, true, nil, true)`; Sampling.measureRanked calls `acrossTies(parts, keys, false, kept, false)`.
- Why it works: adding a part to a tie group shifts every place alike, so no part, hidden or not, reorders the others (except two places typed within 1e-9). For two tied parts the order is unchanged, because the sign already decides.

summary:
Round 2 holds on everything it set out to fix, but one serious problem stands: an invisible duplicate can change a sword's difficulty tier, which the code before the fix (f7ac37d) never allowed.

**The problem.** Matching parts (same size, height and slot) are now ordered from their own middle, and that middle counts hidden parts too. Duplicating a part in place (Ctrl+D) next to a near copy of it, for example a copy nudged 0.001–0.01, changes which copy the analysis keeps.
- C09 with its core typed 2.3 long: Sharpening Hard 0.2110 becomes Normal 0.1967.
- A laminated hilt drops a whole visible plate from the measure: Hammering Normal 0.1175 becomes Hard 0.7000, and cutIndex goes from 0.3971 to 0.6200.
- On every 25th sample sword given such a copy (2,644 swords), G moved on 1,220 and a played tier changed on 71, by up to 0.58.
- f7ac37d and round 1 read all of these the same with or without the duplicate.
- This also makes three SPEC statements false: that a hidden part steers no physics the player is shown, that this class only decides which near copy is kept, and the 'G the same' figures.

**A repair I tried.** Ordering the analysis's matching parts by position instead of by distance from their middle closes every case. It changes nothing on 11,130 sample swords, Parity's 200 or the mirror images. It does move which stacked blade copies are kept on X01, X01raw and X02 (no difficulty change), so 8 tests need adapting or re-recording.

**Everything else held:**
- About 60,000 up/down and front/back moves (snapped, arithmetic, tiny, random, to the edge) and 1,144 whole-sword turns: no difficulty change.
- Mirror images and renumbered parts read as documented.
- Determinism, no NaN or inf, inputs left unchanged.
- The ranking costs about 0.1 ms more per run.
- Of 16 deliberately broken copies, 15 are caught by the tests; the 16th now fails a new test I tried.
- The speed test fails only under load, the same on round 1's code.
